items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. If we constantly rely on the same tools to tell us what to think and how to express it, we risk losing the differences that make [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development.

items.title: UA regents delay statement of intent on AI amid feedback
items.summary:
Work on the university system’s intent language began in 2025, Taylor said, when faculty requested guidance from administration on the use of AI in the classroom.

When complete, the document is designed not to act as policy, but simply to outline the approach the UA institution is taking toward AI, develop guiding principles and put forward expectations of future actions from the administration, including eventually coming up with actual policy. [...] The action was recommended by Chief Technology Officer Benjamin Shier, and pushes off the final decision on the university system’s AI intent language until February, or until requested by UA President Matt Cooper.

Taylor described the feedback being received about the draft “AI Engaged” document as “passionate.” [...] FAIRBANKS, Alaska (KTUU/KTVF) - The University of Alaska (UA) Board of Regents delayed releasing a statement of intent covering the system’s use of artificial intelligence during its November meeting Friday, giving the information technology department time to incorporate feedback from faculty, staff and students into the document.

items.title: Asia not riding but building the AI boom – GIS Reports
items.summary:
The AI ecosystem can be generally separated between three elements: models, compute power and supply chains – with the U.S. and China competing and leading for the first two. Asian countries are looking at how they can stand out amid this intense East-West competition, while capitalizing on their strengths in technology manufacturing supply chains. This has led smaller economies to identify their competitive advantages while investing in novel applications for AI in various industries such as [...] Due to demographic realities, manufacturing and exports are essential to Asian economies. AI is expected to support transitions as each country manages declines in their populations and workforce while maintaining economic growth and prosperity.
